moments: During the Vs. Tour, Pearl Jam would not play Los Angeles on Ticketmaster's terms over service charges. Goldenvoice put them on the Empire Polo Club in Indio instead, for about 25,000 people.
Paul Tollett has said that night showed him what the site could hold (NPR). Wikipedia, citing Billboard in 2012, goes further and says the show 'sowed the seeds' of Coachella.
firsts: Goldenvoice's first show on the grounds
notes: Not a Coachella edition. The 1993 LA Times review was not read; the attendance figure comes from Five Horizons and Wikipedia's citation of it.

attendance: about 17,000-20,000 a day (The Ringer); about 37,000 across both days (Wikipedia, Far Out)
capacity: 'barely more than half' of what Goldenvoice had hoped for (The Ringer); a goal of about 70,000, per Wikipedia
gross: Not reported. The loss was $850,000 (GRAMMY.com) to 'around a million dollars' (Tollett, via The Ringer)
moments: Ran in October heat over 100 degrees. Kid Koala said his vinyl started melting.
Lost money badly. Tom Morello says the festival asked Rage for its fee back and the band gave it; Far Out reports it was half the fee.
Undercard included the Chemical Brothers, Moby, Morrissey, Underworld, DJ Shadow, A Perfect Circle and Jurassic 5. Ninja Tune supplied nine acts.
firsts: First Coachella Valley Music and Arts Festival
Empire Polo Club as the festival site
notes: Morello's wording does not say whether the whole fee or half went back. Wikipedia says Pollstar named it festival of the year; not verified.

dates: Not held (October 2000 dates cancelled, per Wikipedia)
moments: Skipped after the 1999 losses. Per Wikipedia, Tollett blamed too many festivals in Southern California.
Per Wikipedia, Goldenvoice co-staged Pasquale Rotella's Nocturnal Wonderland at the Empire Polo Club in September 2000 instead.
notes: The cancelled dates, the oversaturation reason and the Nocturnal Wonderland swap come only from Wikipedia. The Ringer says only that the loss meant it 'did not return in 2000 at all'.

moments: Moved to spring and cut to one day. Jane's Addiction headlined, with Perry Farrell in a white jumpsuit and fedora.

Rest of the bill: Weezer, The Roots, Mos Def, Gang Starr, Fatboy Slim (closing with a 90-minute set), Paul Oakenfold, the Chemical Brothers (who worked 'Iron Man' into their set), and Sigur Ros (their first Southern California show).
Goldenvoice was sold to AEG in 2001. Wikipedia puts the price at $7 million, for a sale agreed in March; the original report behind that figure was not found.
Whether it made money is disputed. Wikipedia quotes Tollett estimating a 'low, low six-figure' loss; Far Out says it was the year the promoters could finally 'make a profit'.
firsts: First spring (April) edition
First edition after the AEG sale of Goldenvoice
notes: The $65 price, the 32,000 count and the $7M sale price are Wikipedia's. Profit or loss is unsettled; Tollett's line that it took four years to make money (New Yorker, via mxdwn) points to a loss.

headliners: Siouxsie and the Banshees (reunion, per Wikipedia)
moments: Bjork played second-to-last on the Saturday main stage, drew one of the day's biggest crowds and came back for the encore wearing a large green shell on her dress.
The Chemical Brothers closed Saturday, and Oasis played Sunday.
The Sahara tent already had a laser show projected onto circular screens.
firsts: Back to two days
Queens of the Stone Age called the first local Coachella Valley band to play, per Wikipedia
notes: Attendance and the Siouxsie reunion billing are from Wikipedia only. The Daily Bruin confirms a Sahara tent with lasers by 2002, so the Sahara is not a later addition.

attendance: around 30,000 per day (Las Vegas Sun); Wikipedia gives 60,000 total
ga_price: $140 two-day pass; $75 per day, per Wikipedia
moments: Iggy Pop reunited with Ron and Scott Asheton as the Stooges, their first show together in about 30 years. The Las Vegas Sun ranked it second-best of the weekend.
MCA gave an anti-war speech during the Beastie Boys' set, weeks after the invasion of Iraq, and the crowd reaction was mixed.
The White Stripes and Blur also played the main stage. Goldenvoice co-president Rick Van Santen died that December, aged 41, of flu-related complications.
firsts: First on-site camping, per Wikipedia (2,252 sites); OC Weekly calls 2004 'the second year camping was permitted'
notes: The Las Vegas Sun page header shows a 2024 date, but the URL path is 2003/may/02. The 2,252 campsite count is Wikipedia-only.

attendance: about 100,000 over two days, about 50,000 per day (Las Vegas Sun); NPR gives 120,000
ga_price: $75 per day or $142 for both days
moments: The re-formed Pixies played the main stage before Radiohead and, in Rolling Stone's words, 'nearly stole the show.' Beck and the Flaming Lips also played.
Radiohead headlined despite fears they would cancel, but booming bass from the second stage bled into their quieter songs.
Saturday afternoon went past 100 degrees.
firsts: First sellout
notes: The Pixies were billed below the two headliners, not as a headliner. AEG bought half of Coachella in 2004 (The Ringer). Wikipedia says Tollett regrets not adding a third day for Bowie; not verified.

headliners: New Order (Sunday closer after NIN, per Rolling Stone)
attendance: about 50,000 per day expected (Las Vegas Sun); Rolling Stone estimated 50,000
capacity: not sold out at press time (Las Vegas Sun, Apr 29)
ga_price: $81 per day or $152 for two days
moments: Arcade Fire played Sunday on the Outdoor Stage. Rolling Stone called the set 'galvanizing' and said it drew a massive crowd.

Bauhaus played together for the first time since 1998, with Peter Murphy hanging upside down during 'Bela Lugosi's Dead'. Gang of Four's original lineup played its first North American show since 1981.
Coldplay's 'Yellow' turned into a crowd singalong.
notes: The lineup had 92 acts on five stages. Wikipedia says a Cocteau Twins reunion was cancelled; not checked.

attendance: more than 100,000 over two days (Billboard); Wikipedia gives 120,000
moments: Daft Punk debuted the LED pyramid in the Sahara tent at 11 p.m. Saturday. Water & Music traces a live-production 'arms race' from the set.
The story that 40,000 people tried to get into a tent built for 10,000 comes from the band's manager, in Daft Punk Unchained. Nobody counted.
Madonna played the Sahara the next day, came on about 20 minutes late to boos, and did about six songs. Billboard called it a fun novelty but a logistical nightmare.
Kanye West, Massive Attack (with Liz Fraser), Gnarls Barkley and Scissor Sisters were also on the bill.
firsts: Daft Punk pyramid live debut
notes: Ticket price not verified. Daft Punk's fee was $300K according to Daft Punk Unchained (2015), or $350K plus travel according to Goldenvoice's own 2024 film.

capacity: the first two days stayed on sale until the gates opened; day three 'had sold out instantly' (Diffuser)
moments: Rage Against the Machine closed Sunday, Apr 29, their first show since splitting in 2000. They opened with 'Testify', and Zack de la Rocha made a political statement during 'Wake Up'.
The story of a campground riot after the Rage set, with helicopters and SWAT nearby, comes from one OC Weekly writer's 2018 history built from attendee forum posts. No police report was found.
firsts: First three-day Coachella
Stagecoach country festival launched on the same grounds that spring
notes: Dancing Astronaut, citing Billboard, gives 'about $16 million' and '62,000 attendees' (likely a daily figure); neither was checked against Boxscore.

moments: Prince headlined Saturday, Apr 26, with an eight-minute cover of Radiohead's 'Creep', and brought out Sheila E. His team had the fan videos taken down. A December 2015 upload he tweeted was pulled again days later by his own publisher.
Roger Waters played Dark Side of the Moon. The inflatable pig was let go and floated off into the night.
Tollett says this was the year he lost the most money, with Stagecoach spending at the same time.
notes: Tollett told the LA Times in 2019: 'I lost a lot of money in 2008.' Prince's reported fee ($4-5M in listicles) is unverified.

ga_price: $269 three-day (layaway plan offered); $120 single day at the door
moments: Paul McCartney opened the festival on Friday with a two-and-a-half-hour set and two encores. Per Wikipedia, he ran 54 minutes past curfew.
Per Wikipedia, the Cure's set was cut off after running about 30 minutes past curfew. Leonard Cohen made a rare appearance.
firsts: First payment plan for passes, offered in the recession; about 19% of festivalgoers used it

sources.publication: Associated Press via The Washington Times

notes: The curfew overrun figures are from Wikipedia.

attendance: about 75,000 per day (UPI); 225,000 aggregate, per Wikipedia
capacity: all 75,000 three-day passes sold out in advance (BizBash)
moments: Overcrowding: LA Weekly reported gate-crashing, fistfights and 'near-riot' conditions at the gates on Friday, counterfeit tickets, three-hour entry waits, and a near-crush at an exit on Sunday. Tollett said in 2011: 'The mistakes were in the planning.'
The Eyjafjallajokull volcanic ash cloud stranded seven acts in England.
Jay-Z brought out Beyonce as a surprise guest.
firsts: First year selling three-day passes only, on nontransferable wristbands (BizBash)
Ferris wheel on site by this year (BizBash)
Car camping beside your tent (Phoenix New Times)
Webcast of one act at a time, behind a Wrigley Facebook 'like' (CNET; the multistage YouTube stream came in 2011)
notes: 'The crush' was overcrowding and gate-crashing. No mass-casualty crowd crush was reported. UPI counted 69 arrests over the weekend.

attendance: 225,000 aggregate, 75,000 paid per day, per Wikipedia; Tollett would not announce capacity in advance
ga_price: $269 three-day plus fees (resale at $400 and up)
moments: Fixes after 2010: bigger grounds and tents, and a tamper-proof chipped wristband scanned on the approach and again at the gates.
YouTube streamed three stages on separate channels, about 60 bands over three days with Wrigley as sponsor, and nearly 4 million people watched.
On May 31, 2011, Goldenvoice announced a second identical weekend for 2012.
firsts: First full YouTube livestream
notes: The Strokes were also top-billed. Wikipedia lists 'Kanye West / The Strokes'.

attendance: 158,387 paid across both weekends (80,726 + 77,661), per Wikipedia citing Billboard Boxscore
capacity: W1 sold out in about 40 minutes, W2 'within another two hours' (mxdwn)
gross: $47,313,403, per Wikipedia citing Billboard Boxscore; GRAMMY.com gives $47.3M
moments: The Tupac 'hologram' during Dr. Dre and Snoop Dogg's set on Apr 15 was Pepper's ghost, projected onto Mylar foil. Digital Domain built the digital Tupac, AV Concepts projected it, and it was Dre's idea.
First year with two weekends. Tollett preferred cloning the festival to adding about 40,000 people a day.
firsts: First two-weekend year
notes: This corrects an implied $315 GA (from Wikipedia's '$349, up $34'): the advertised 2012 price was $285 plus fees. Dancing Astronaut notes that 2013 prices no longer carried the extra service charges, which may explain the gap. The 2012 gross was not seen in a Billboard source directly. The $10M Tupac cost is an unattributed rumor.

moments: Poetic Kinetics brought Helix Poeticus, a moving snail about 30 ft tall and 80 ft long, built on a forklift.
Indio approved a deal keeping the festival there through at least 2030 and raising the city's per-ticket share from $2.33 to $5.01 starting in 2014.
firsts: Yuma tent opened as the sixth stage
Sahara tent expanded, per Wikipedia
notes: No single defining moment was verified in this pass.

attendance: 96,500 per day, 579,000 admissions across six days (Billboard via SPIN)
vip_price: over $5,000, per Wikipedia (likely a premium package, not standard VIP)
gross: $78,332,000 (Billboard via SPIN), the third straight record year
moments: Outkast reunited for their first shows in about a decade, with Janelle Monae and Future as guests. It was the first stop of a 20th-anniversary run of more than 40 festivals. Billboard called it 'imperfect'.
Heineken House replaced the sponsor's domes, with sets by Skrillex, Outkast and Lorde. AXS TV broadcast weekend two, per Wikipedia.
firsts: TV broadcast of weekend 2 on AXS TV, per Wikipedia
Heineken House
notes: Wikipedia calls the 579,000 figure a typo. It is not: it is cumulative daily admissions (96,500 x 6). Unique attendees would be about a third of that. The 'most-tweeted moment' claim for Outkast was not confirmed.

moments: On weekend one Sunday, Apr 12, Madonna joined Drake's set for three songs and kissed him. His recoil went viral.
AC/DC headlined Friday despite online grumbling, and LAist said the whole crowd sang along.
firsts: SiriusXM broadcast, per Wikipedia
notes: The PDF is a third-party mirror of the Pollstar chart.

capacity: 100% sold (Pollstar). In April 2016 Indio's council approved raising the daily cap from 99,000 to 125,000, phased in
gross: $94,218,000 (Pollstar 2016 year-end; the chart misprints it as '$94,218,0000')
moments: Guns N' Roses with Slash and Duff McKagan: Axl Rose had broken his foot and performed seated on a guitar-studded throne built by Dave Grohl. He brought out Angus Young the day his move to AC/DC as frontman was announced.
Weekend two included tributes to Prince, who died Apr 21, 2016, per Wikipedia.
firsts: Despacio sound system
Same year Goldenvoice staged Desert Trip on the grounds in October; Tollett told The New York Times it would gross about $160M

sources.publication: Live for Live Music, citing The New York Times

notes: The 125,000 cap is a ceiling, not a count. Wikipedia also lists an N.W.A reunion with Ice Cube on weekend one; not verified here.

gross: $114,593,000 (Pollstar). The first recurring festival to gross over $100M (Billboard via Dancing Astronaut)
moments: Beyonce withdrew on doctors' advice during her pregnancy, and Lady Gaga took the Saturday slot. On Apr 15 Gaga debuted 'The Cure' live and released it that night.
Radiohead's Friday weekend-one set lost sound at least four times, starting during 'Ful Stop'. Thom Yorke joked about aliens.
Tollett told The New Yorker each headliner was paid $3-4M.
firsts: La Grande XL Ferris wheel debuted, replacing the original La Grande wheel
Sonora tent
Antarctic projection dome
First recurring festival over $100M gross
notes: Scenes for A Star Is Born were filmed here, per Wikipedia; not verified. The Anschutz anti-LGBTQ donations story broke in Jan 2017 (The FADER, 2017-01-05).

capacity: daily cap of up to 125,000 under Indio's 2016 vote, phased in (Pollstar); a ceiling, not a count
moments: Beychella: Beyonce headlined both Saturdays, Apr 14 and Apr 21, the first Black woman to headline. The show was built as an HBCU homecoming with about 200 people on stage, plus a Destiny's Child reunion, Jay-Z and Solange. Netflix released Homecoming on Apr 17, 2019.
40 mph winds kept the weekend-two campgrounds closed until 3 a.m. Friday, and many campers waited in a Walmart parking lot (OC Weekly).
firsts: First Black woman headliner
Record of about 458,000 concurrent YouTube viewers for Beyonce's weekend-one set (TMZ, via The FADER)
notes: GRAMMY.com gives 'April 13 and 22', which is wrong: she played the Saturday slots, Apr 14 and Apr 21. Wikipedia reports booking fees around $8M and Teen Vogue harassment reporting; not verified.

moments: Ariana Grande, at 25, was the youngest headliner (AFP). On Apr 14 she brought out four members of NSYNC and sang Justin Timberlake's parts herself; Diddy, Mase and Nicki Minaj also came out.

Kanye West walked away from a headline slot in January after asking late for a custom dome stage, and Grande got the slot. He held a public Sunday Service on Easter, Apr 21, on a hill built in the campground between weekends.
Lead rigger Christopher Griffin, 49, a 20-year Goldenvoice employee, died in a fall from scaffolding during setup. Solange cancelled a week before.
firsts: Both weekends livestreamed on YouTube for the first time (USA Today, via Wikipedia)
20th edition
notes: GA sold out in about 40 minutes and all passes in six hours (IQ). Justin Bieber guested with Ariana on weekend two (widely reported; not fetched). Sunday Service had been invite-only since January.

dates: Cancelled (scheduled Apr 10-12 and Apr 17-19; moved to October, then cancelled)
moments: Postponed to October in March 2020 over COVID-19, then cancelled in June 2020 by Riverside County's public health officer, Dr. Cameron Kaiser.
The documentary 'Coachella: 20 Years in the Desert' premiered on YouTube on Apr 10, 2020.
firsts: First cancellation since the skipped 2000
notes: The exact October dates were not verified.

moments: Cancelled again. Riverside County's public health officer cancelled the April dates in January 2021.
Aug 2021: Indio's council voted 3-1 to extend its festival deal to 2050. Oct 2021: Goldenvoice signed a lease with the Haagen family for the Empire Polo Club running to 2050.

headliners: Swedish House Mafia and The Weeknd (replacing Ye)
attendance: not reported. Variety, via Wikipedia, reported that Styles' opening-night crowd topped 100,000
moments: Ye dropped out about Apr 4, less than two weeks before. Swedish House Mafia and The Weeknd were announced as replacements on Apr 6.
On the first Friday Harry Styles brought out Shania Twain and played 'As It Was' live for the first time. Lizzo joined him on weekend two.

First edition after the pandemic. Rage Against the Machine and Travis Scott (removed after Astroworld) were carried over from 2020 and didn't play. 2NE1 performed together for the first time in six years, and Brockhampton played their final shows.
firsts: 88rising's 'Head in the Clouds Forever', in Billboard's words 'the first label-curated set ever to hit the festival's main stage'
notes: Billie Eilish (20) would beat Ariana (25) as youngest headliner, but no source confirming the claim was found. Check before publishing.

capacity: weekend 2 did not sell out, the first time since 2012 (Desert Sun)
moments: Bad Bunny opened Friday as the first Latin artist to headline. Post Malone joined for 'La Cancion'.
BLACKPINK became the first K-pop group billed as headliners. All three headliners were nonwhite, a first.

Frank Ocean came on about an hour late and the planned ice-rink segment never happened; a source told Rolling Stone he had hurt his ankle in rehearsals. He withdrew from weekend two citing two fractures and a sprain in his left leg, and Blink-182 took his slot.
Indio fined Goldenvoice $117,000 for curfew overruns on weekend one alone.
firsts: First Latin headliner
First K-pop headliner
First all-nonwhite headliner slate
notes: Some outlets called BLACKPINK the first Asian headliner; the careful sources say K-pop. Billboard, as reported by The FADER, put Ocean's contract at $8M for both weekends and said weekend-one production cost more than his $4M fee, with the festival standing to lose 'several million dollars'. The rink's own cost is unconfirmed. Skrillex, Fred again.. and Four Tet used the rink on weekend two.

capacity: about 80% of 250,000 sold by opening day (Billboard); weekend 2 never fully sold out (Pollstar)
moments: SFGate called it the 'slowest ticket sales in ten years'. Weekend one took nearly a month to sell out, and Billboard's sources put sales down 14-17% year over year.
No Doubt played their first show in nearly a decade, with Olivia Rodrigo joining for 'Bathwater'.
Billie Eilish joined Lana Del Rey for 'Ocean Eyes' and 'Video Games'.
notes: Stagecoach 2024 (89,003) outsold each Coachella weekend. The KESQ counts (about 81K per weekend) are far below the 125K daily cap and may cover only the tickets the city collects a fee on.

attendance: about 120,000 per weekend, about 240,000 total (NBC Palm Springs); the state alcohol regulator counted daily peaks of nearly 110,000; Wikipedia gives about 245,000
capacity: W1 GA gone by Dec 2024; W2 'widely available', reselling for as little as $246 by April
ga_price: $549 at Dec 2024 tier; $649 W1 / $599 W2 by April 2025
moments: Lady Gaga debuted the Mayhem show, a 'demonic opera house' set in four acts and a finale. Per Wikipedia, she was the second woman to headline twice, after Bjork.
Green Day's Coachella debut included a 'not part of the MAGA agenda' line. Travis Scott built 'The Village by Cactus Jack'.
The LA Philharmonic, conducted by Gustavo Dudamel, became the first classical orchestra to play (Apr 12).
firsts: First classical orchestra (LA Phil), per Wikipedia
YouTube dedicated Coachella livestream app (Sherwood News)
notes: The Go-Go's played their first show since 2022. Charli XCX brought out Lorde, Billie Eilish and Troye Sivan. On Apr 18 deadmau5 left a set early and posted 'Probably my last Coachella.'

capacity: GA and VIP for both weekends sold out about three days after the Sep 2025 on-sale (VICE)
moments: Justin Bieber headlined Saturday on a deal he negotiated himself. Rolling Stone, citing one unnamed source, reported a fee 'north of $10 million'. On weekend two SZA and Sexyy Red came out, and he serenaded Billie Eilish.
Karol G became the first Latina headliner. Madonna joined Sabrina Carpenter on weekend two for three songs, timed to her new single.
Radiohead did not play. The poster's 'bunker' was their KID A MNESIA Motion Picture House, about 17,000 sq ft underground, on a foundation Indio's assessors valued at $2.5M.

Wind cancelled Anyma's weekend-one Friday set; he played a Do LaB b2b that Sunday and moved his full show to weekend two. TMZ put weekend two's curfew fines at $44,000. The Strokes closed Apr 18 with visuals condemning strikes on Iran and Gaza.
firsts: First Latina headliner (Karol G)
First time three pop acts headlined (Pollstar)
Underground art venue on the grounds
notes: The 25th edition. The lineup was announced on Sep 15, 2025, about four months earlier than usual. In Sep 2026 YouTube extended its exclusive livestream deal through 2030 and said the 2026 stream set its concurrent-viewer record, without a number. Latin Post's $220-240M gross claim is unsourced.
